meta.title: How project work becomes a useful lesson

learningObjective: Explain how the skill separates adaptive teaching content from a stable renderer, and identify why that separation makes the result safer to update.

summary.whatHappened: The project was split into a small teaching skill, structured lesson data, and a stable HTML renderer.
summary.whyItMatters: The agent can adapt explanations to each learner without redesigning the page or weakening accessibility on every run.
summary.whatChanged: Learning goals, project evidence, review questions, and visual descriptions now enter one validated data format before they become a lesson.
summary.whatToLearn: Separate variable content from fixed presentation when one part needs to adapt and the other needs to stay predictable.
summary.verification: The package tests validate the lesson data, render the page, and check its quiz and responsive layout. The optional network 3D enhancement is not required for the lesson.

learningDiff.softwareChange: The skill now separates its short learning brief from the agent response with a fixed end marker, then uses structured learning data for deeper practice.
learningDiff.whyItWorks: A stable boundary lets the learner stop after the brief or continue into detail without confusing the two layers.
learningDiff.mentalModel: Separate a small predictable interface from the richer system behind it. The boundary makes each part easier to use and test.
canNow: Identify where the learning brief ends and the normal response begins
Explain why validated content and a stable renderer can evolve independently
learningDiff.verificationLimits: The validator and renderer are covered by package tests. A rendered browser check is still needed to verify the visible boundary and practice interaction.

evidence: SKILL.md defines when and how the agent teaches.
validate_lesson.py rejects incomplete or disallowed lesson copy.
render_lesson.py creates one self-contained HTML page with an offline fallback.

beforeAfter.before: An agent could generate a different page structure and visual style for every lesson.
beforeAfter.after: The agent generates validated lesson data, then one renderer applies the same readable structure and accessibility rules.
beforeAfter.reason: A stable boundary makes both content adaptation and interface testing easier to reason about.

concepts.name: Separate content from presentation
concepts.plainExplanation: Content is the meaning of the lesson. Presentation is the layout and interaction used to communicate it. Keeping them separate lets each change for a clear reason.
concepts.projectExample: The agent writes the summary and questions in JSON. The renderer decides typography, spacing, keyboard behavior, and the visual fallback.

concepts.name: Use project evidence as the source
concepts.plainExplanation: An explanation becomes useful when it points to the actual decision, file, test, or behavior that produced it.
concepts.projectExample: This lesson cites the schema, validator, renderer, and package tests instead of describing an imaginary application.

concepts.name: Make enhancement optional
concepts.plainExplanation: A richer feature should not remove the basic path. If it fails, the learner still needs the full explanation.
concepts.projectExample: The 3D view loads only after a button press. A labeled static relationship remains visible before and after that choice.

projectTrace.label: Skill contract
projectTrace.reason: Defines the maximum 30-second brief and its required end marker.

projectTrace.label: Validator
projectTrace.reason: Rejects overlong briefs and incomplete open-response practice.

projectTrace.label: Renderer
projectTrace.reason: Displays the boundary and requires an attempt before guidance is revealed.

visualizations.title: From project work to lesson
visualizations.description: The lesson is created through a short sequence with a validation boundary.
nodes: Inspect the current request and project evidence
Adapt to the learner's objective and prior records
Validate tone, completeness, and quiz answers
Render and test the offline lesson

visualizations.title: Three parts with different jobs
visualizations.description: The conversation informs the content, project evidence keeps it factual, and the renderer makes it readable.

quiz.question: The learner changes their goal from understanding tests to understanding architecture. Which part should change first?
choices: The page typography and keyboard controls
quiz.explanation: The goal changes what the lesson teaches. The stable renderer should keep its readability and interaction rules.

quiz.question: The Three.js module cannot load while the learner is offline. What should happen?
choices: The lesson should stop until the connection returns
The static relationship and complete text explanation should remain usable
quiz.explanation: The rich view is optional. The static and text paths carry the same learning meaning without a network request.

quiz.question: If the renderer did not show a fixed end marker after the short brief, what confusion could that create for the learner?
quiz.guidance: Consider the learner who wants only the quick understanding and the learner who wants the full technical response.
quiz.modelAnswer: The learner could not reliably tell which information belongs to the promised short learning artifact and which belongs to the normal agent response. That makes the time promise unclear and makes the format harder to scan.
quiz.explanation: The fixed marker is an interface boundary. It gives both reading paths a predictable point of separation.

recallPrompt: Without looking at the lesson, explain why a fixed boundary between the learning brief and detailed response improves both usability and testing.
transferQuestion: Where else in your current project could separating variable content from stable presentation make future changes easier to test?
